question: Was Jesus taken to Caiaphas or Annas first?
summary: Matthew 26:57 names Caiaphas explicitly as the high priest Jesus was led to. Mark 14:53 and Luke 22:54 say Jesus was led to 'the high priest,' which in context means Caiaphas, since he was the sitting high priest in 30-36 CE. John 18:13 alone has Jesus taken first to *Annas*, Caiaphas's father-in-law, before being sent to Caiaphas in 18:24. Three gospels go straight to Caiaphas; John inserts an extra hearing before Annas.

reconcile.connective: Defenders read John's Annas stop and the Synoptics' Caiaphas trial as one continuous custody in stages — a preliminary hearing before the deposed but still-powerful Annas, who then sends Jesus on to his son-in-law Caiaphas.

discrepancy.connective: D. F. Strauss treats the Fourth Gospel's distinctive trial sequence — the unique detour to Annas absent from the other three — as one of John's departures from the Synoptic single hearing, not a detail the accounts straightforwardly share.

skeptic.name: David Friedrich Strauss
skeptic.work: The Life of Jesus Critically Examined
skeptic.attribution: David Friedrich Strauss (d. 1874), The Life of Jesus Critically Examined, trans. George Eliot (1846; German orig. 1835)

pd_work.resource: John Haley, An Examination of the Alleged Discrepancies of the Bible (1874)
pd_work.author: John Haley
pd_work.note: Haley treats the Annas/Caiaphas trial sequence under the harmonizing tradition, arguing John's 'first to Annas' supplies a preliminary stage the Synoptics omit rather than a rival claim.

link.title: CARM: Who did Jesus see first upon His arrest, Annas or Caiaphas?
link.note: live apologetic treatment harmonizing Matthew 26:57 and John 18:13 as sequential hearings

excerpts.excerpt_text: The Gospels record Jesus as undergoing five hearings: (1) an informal hearing before Annas (John 18:13-24); (2) a night hearing before the Sanhedrin (Matt 26:59-66); (3) a morning hearing before the Sanhedrin (27:1-2); (4) a hearing before Herod Antipas (Luke 23:6-12); and (5) a two-stage trial before Pilate (Matt 27:11-31; see Luke 23:6-12). It all amounts to two trials, a Jewish trial and a Roman trial.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly dissolves the tension by listing the Annas hearing (John) and the Caiaphas/Sanhedrin hearing as distinct, sequential stages of one process rather than competing claims about where Jesus went first.
excerpts.source_note_text:
26:57–27:26 The Gospels record Jesus as undergoing five hearings: (1) an informal hearing before Annas (John 18:13-24); (2) a night hearing before the Sanhedrin (Matt 26:59-66); (3) a morning hearing before the Sanhedrin (27:1-2); (4) a hearing before Herod Antipas (Luke 23:6-12); and (5) a two-stage trial before Pilate (Matt 27:11-31; see Luke 23:6-12). It all amounts to two trials, a Jewish trial and a Roman trial.
26:57-68 This hearing might have been little more than an unofficial preliminary hearing designed to establish consensus on the terms of the charges. The Jewish leaders were under considerable pressure to keep this incident secret, lest their actions cause a riot (see 21:26, 46; 26:5, 55; John 11:45-53).
